A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SODP research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original SODP results on Meta-World and Adroit, learning curves, regularization and pre-training ablations, and per-task returns in Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds baseline evaluations, limited-data experiments, transfer experiments, visual Meta-World results, and further ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same diffusion pre-training, policy-gradient fine-tuning, and proficient-trajectory BC regularization procedure. Visual Meta-World uses the encoder approach already employed for Adroit; the newly disclosed regularization weight does not establish a method change.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates state-based Meta-World and visual Adroit. v2 additionally evaluates image/point-cloud Meta-World MT-10, extending visual manipulation coverage to ten Sawyer tasks using collected visual data (Appendix C.4, Table 8). Both original evaluation settings remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated RLPD, IBRL, Cal-QL, MTSAC, and MTDQL comparisons while retaining the earlier comparator rows. In particular, the first three substantially broaden comparison to methods combining offline pre-training with online fine-tuning.

E3.justification: The original main training budgets remain, but v2 introduces substantial new protocols: 100k-step online fine-tuning with augmented-data controls for offline baselines (Section 5.3), MT-10 versus basketball pre-training for held-out tasks (Section 5.5), offline fine-tuning using 200 successful episodes per task, and equal-size comparisons of pre-training data quality (Appendices C.1 and C.3).

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of online versus offline fine-tuning and training from scratch on high-quality data (Table 4), BC-only fine-tuning (Table 5), pre-training data quality (Table 6), and multi-task versus single-task pre-training for transfer (Table 3). The original scratch and BC/KL/PL regularization ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain three-seed mean/standard-deviation reporting, five-seed comparative learning curves, and per-task return statistics over 50 episodes. Additional result tables use the existing uncertainty-reporting approach; no new statistical testing or revised repeated-run practice is documented.

E6.justification: Shared Table 1 scores, Adroit results, and appendix per-task returns are unchanged. v2 adds substantial results, including SODP's 59.26% success under the 100k-step protocol (Table 2), 80.93% after near-optimal versus 65.27% after sub-optimal pre-training (Table 6), and 47.5% on visual MT-10 (Table 8). These are newly reported settings, not improvements over v1 under identical conditions.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, policy-gradient and importance-sampling derivations, NLL surrogate derivation in Appendix A, and regularization formulas remain mathematically unchanged. Shortened sampling notation and omission of the explicit noise-reconstruction expression do not alter the retained definitions or reasoning.

C1.justification: The central claims remain learning from task-agnostic sub-optimal data, efficient reward-guided adaptation, and superior downstream manipulation performance. The added experiments support these existing claims. Adroit remains in the abstract and evaluation despite being omitted from the introduction's contribution summary.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation beyond the original regularization and pre-training discussion. It attributes offline-online baseline failures to biased value learning and inadequate multimodal priors, explains differing responses to augmented data, and interprets offline fine-tuning and transfer results. Appendix C.4 also adds the qualification that Adroit hammer may require stronger pre-training priors.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 newly specifies the BC weight as lambda = 1.0. Appendices C.4 and D add visual Meta-World data-collection instructions and implementation sources and architecture details for new baselines. Core SODP implementation details remain, although v1's explicit disclosure that Adroit baselines use expert demonstrations is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations and positioning for RLPD, IBRL, and Cal-QL, connecting SODP more directly to offline-online RL. The broader diffusion literature discussion and comparison with DPPO remain substantially unchanged. Updated bibliographic entries for existing works do not represent additional research coverage.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially reorganized around offline-online comparisons, limited-sample efficiency, and transfer. Existing Adroit results, pre-training ablations, multi-task learning curves, and longer regularization explanations move into organized appendix sections. The introduction receives localized edits, while the method and conclusion remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: The main text changes from predominantly single-column to two-column layout. v2 expands Table 1, adds six result tables and a new learning-curve figure, and relocates several existing displays. All original figures remain, including v1 Figure 4 as v2 Figure 8. Algorithm 1 is compressed into fewer, less clearly separated lines.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical support beyond v1's primarily offline comparisons. Offline-online baselines and the augmented-data control in Section 5.3 address whether SODP's advantage merely reflects additional online experience. Transfer experiments and targeted appendix ablations better test generalizability and the fine-tuning mechanism. These gains outweigh limited reporting regressions, including the now-inaccurate statement that MTBC performs worst in Table 1 and less explicit Adroit baseline training-data disclosure.
